I've been working this land for 55 years. My hands know what to do before my head finishes thinking. Let me go through what I'll do this year.

**Wheat** — I plant wheat every October on most of my land, 7.5 mu. I'll use the same improved variety I've used for several years now — the seed station sells it and it handles the dry spells here in Quzhou better than the old stuff my father used. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the plants joint in spring. I irrigate four times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots, once at jointing, once at heading, once filling out the grain. Three rounds of spraying — herbicide early on, then aphids and powdery mildew in spring. I expect around 450 jin per mu, same as most years.

**Maize** — Same 7.5 mu, right after wheat harvest in June. I direct-seed hybrid maize, no ploughing, the soil is fine from the wheat rotation. My son used to help me with this but he's in the city now so I hire a seeder. I put fertilizer down with the seed and top-dress urea at tasseling. Summer rains usually come, so I only need to pump the well twice — at planting if it's dry, and at silking. One herbicide spray, one for corn borer. I figure around 550 jin per mu.

**Cotton** — I keep 2.6 mu in cotton on the separate plot. It's hard work at my age, lots of bending and spraying, but cotton money is still good and I've grown it my whole life. I plough that plot in spring, use hybrid seed, and plant in late April. Cotton drinks water so I pump four times across the season. The bollworm and aphids mean I spray five or six times — that's just the cost of cotton. I put more potassium in cotton than the other crops, it needs it. I expect about 300 jin of seed cotton per mu.

My household is big but it's mostly the young ones who've left. My wife and I manage what we can. I'm not changing anything dramatic this year — at 73, what works, works.
